label: first copy step after <DEL> (outputting orig[1]), when the upcoming tokens include n/w/v/o/x/l/k/2
explanation: Position-locked feature. Nearly all activations (99.7% of steps, 99.8% of mass) are at step L+1, the first copy step after <DEL>: the input is orig[0] fed back and the model is outputting orig[1]. It almost never fires in the original phase, on <DEL>, or at later copy steps. It is active on only about 16% of those steps, though, and which ones depends on the upcoming tokens. It fires most often and hardest when orig[1] or orig[2] is in {n, w, v, o, x, l, k, 2}. n and w have the highest lift (out_tok w/n about 6.5x, next_out n 8.6x). The top activations look like "y n n n n 1" and "q w n n r", where w or n is at orig[1] and n n follows. The rate drops as the sequence has more digits, and it is highest at L = 5-6. Gating on recall_idx == 1 alone gives recall 0.997 but precision 0.16. Adding the token-set condition raises precision to only about 0.28, so which content selects the active steps is not fully captured.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: recall_idx=1 (+4.59), prev_tok=<DEL> (+4.59), orig2=n (+4.05), orig4=n (+3.63), orig3=n (+3.61), orig1=n (+2.87). Lower it: to_go=1 (-3.90), in_first=1 (-3.56), L=9 (-3.30), orig3=b (-3.06).
